name: ec-mulgen-linear
note: CONSTANT-OPERAND PRECONDITION: this rewrite fires only when BOTH scalars resolve to compile-time constants; the sum is then folded mod n at rewrite time. Runtime (non-constant) scalars are left alone. That is not an arbitrary limit — it is what makes the seven tiers agree byte-for-byte. All six hand-written tiers (ts, rust, python, zig, ruby, java) guard on getConstInt/get_const_int; the Go engine is data-driven off this file and used to fire the rule unconditionally, emitting a plain bin_op '+' helper for runtime scalars. The script it produced was VALID (emitEcMulGen/emitEcMul reduce the scalar mod n before the ladder — emitScalarReduce in ec-codegen.ts / ecEmitScalarReduce in codegen/ec.go — so an unreduced k1 + k2 never reached the ladder unreduced) but it was a DIFFERENT script from every other tier for the same source, which conformance invariant 2 forbids. The Go guard now lives in opOperandsAreConst (compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go). NOTE this means the scalar reduce is no longer load-bearing FOR THIS RULE; it remains load-bearing in its own right because unlock-argument scalars are attacker-chosen and may be >= n or negative (see ec-scalar-domain.test.ts). The k1 + k2 = 0 (mod n) case agrees with the unrewritten spelling only because affineAdd returns the all-zero point for P + (-P); see the P == -Q comment in ec-codegen.ts. Pinned by ec-mulgen-linear-parity.test.ts (TS/Go hex parity for both the runtime and the constant shape) and by TestECOptimizer_MulGenLinearSkipsRuntimeScalars in compilers/go/frontend.
